G-F071.trick: SYNOVIAL = a joint with a fluid-filled "bubble" (cavity) wrapped in a capsule.
G-F071.tip: Cavity + capsule + cartilage + fluid = synovial. Fibrous and cartilaginous joints have no cavity.

G-F072.trick: LIGAMENTS Link bone to bone. TENDONS Tie muscle to bone.
G-F072.tip: Ligament vs tendon is a favorite distractor. Bone-to-bone always means ligament.

G-F073.trick: PIVOT = shaking your head "no" at the atlas and axis.
G-F073.tip: Rotation around one axis = pivot (atlas–axis, radius–ulna). A hinge only bends and straightens.

G-F074.trick: Ball-and-socket = a joystick: moves every direction and can draw circles.
G-F074.tip: Only the shoulder and hip are ball-and-socket. They allow movement in all planes plus rotation.

G-F075.trick: ABduction = ABduct (take away) from the body. ADDuction = ADD back to the body.
G-F075.tip: Movement away from the midline is abduction. Picture doing a jumping jack.

G-F076.trick: SUPination = holding a bowl of SOUP. Pronation = palm down, pouring it out.
G-F076.tip: Supination = palm up (anatomical position). Pronation = palm down.

G-F077.trick: DORSiflexion = toes up toward the DORSum (top), like walking on your heels.
G-F077.tip: Dorsiflexion = top of foot toward shin. Plantar flexion = pointing toes, like pressing a gas pedal.

G-F078.trick: Menisci = shock-absorbing cushions that make the round femur sit better on the flat tibia.
G-F078.tip: Menisci spread the load and improve fit. Ligaments, not menisci, are the main stabilizers.

G-F079.trick: Hip = a deep cup (acetabulum) for stability. Shoulder = a shallow saucer for range of motion.
G-F079.tip: Weight-bearing joints trade mobility for stability. The hip is more stable but less mobile than the shoulder.

G-F080.trick: Cartilage has no blood supply, so its repair crew can't get there.
G-F080.tip: Avascular tissues heal slowly. That's why cartilage damage (like osteoarthritis) tends to progress.

C-ch8-overview.trick: FUNCTIONAL = how much it FUNCTIONS (moves). STRUCTURAL = what it's made of.
C-ch8-overview.tip: Words about movement (freely, slightly, immovable) = functional classification.

C-ch8-functional.trick: Syn = Stuck, Amphi = A bit, Di = Do anything (synarthrosis, amphiarthrosis, diarthrosis).
C-ch8-functional.tip: "Slightly movable" = amphiarthrotic. Watch out for structural words like "synovial" in a functional question.

C-ch8-fibrous.trick: GOMPHOSIS = a tooth bolted (gomphos = bolt) into its socket.
C-ch8-fibrous.tip: Fibrous joints: suture (skull), syndesmosis (ligament between bones), gomphosis (tooth).

C-ch8-cartilaginous.trick: SynCHONDROsis = joined by hyaline cartilage (chondro). SymPHYSIS = fibrocartilage pad.
C-ch8-cartilaginous.tip: Epiphyseal plate and first rib–sternum = synchondrosis. Pubic symphysis and discs = symphysis.

C-ch8-synovial-structure.trick: BURSA = a little purse (bursa) of fluid that stops rubbing.
C-ch8-synovial-structure.tip: Kneeling pain over the kneecap suggests bursitis. Bursae reduce friction between skin, tendon and bone.

C-ch8-types.trick: Wide circles + rotation = ball-and-socket (hip or shoulder).
C-ch8-types.tip: Circumduction plus rotation narrows it to ball-and-socket joints.

C-ch8-movements.trick: Heels down, toes up = DORSiflexion (toward the top/dorsum).
C-ch8-movements.tip: Standing on heels = dorsiflexion. Standing on tiptoes = plantar flexion.

C-ch8-examples.trick: ACL = Anterior Cruciate: stops the tibia from sliding Anteriorly (forward).
C-ch8-examples.tip: Name tells direction: the anterior cruciate stops forward slide; the posterior cruciate stops backward slide.

C-ch8-aging.trick: Aging cartilage is like an old sponge: drier and stiffer.
C-ch8-aging.tip: Gradual stiffness with no injury in older adults points to normal aging of cartilage and collagen.

C-ch8-disorders.trick: Tick + bull's-eye rash + swollen knee = Lyme.
C-ch8-disorders.tip: Clue words decide arthritis type: tick (Lyme), autoimmune (RA), uric acid (gout), wear-and-tear (OA).

C-ch8-summary.trick: AMPHI = A bit of movement. Discs and the pubic symphysis give a little.
C-ch8-summary.tip: Both answers must match. Rule out any pair that includes a freely movable (synovial) joint.
